title: Pseudo-coherent complexes of finite Tor dimension over a ring are perfect
statement: Let R be a ring and let C be an object of the derived category D(R) [def-pc-derived-category]. Assume C is pseudo-coherent, meaning that it admits a quasi-isomorphism from a bounded-above complex of finitely generated projective R-modules. Assume also that C has finite Tor dimension: there are integers a <= b such that H^i(C tensor_R^L M) = 0 for every R-module M and every i outside [a,b]. Then C is quasi-isomorphic to a bounded complex of finitely generated projective R-modules, hence is perfect in the affine sense of [def-pc-perfect-complex].

proof.text: Unfold [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex] in hPC to obtain a finite-free complex P with P.IsStrictlyLE c and Q.obj P isomorphic to C. Convert each free term to a flat module with ModuleCat.flat_iff_flat. Apply the closed upstream CochainComplex.kFlat_of_isStrictlyLE_of_flat directly over R. No replacement with prescribed upper Tor bound is needed, since the conclusion only asks for some finite bounds.

The closed upstream DerivedCategory.homologyConcentratedIn_of_torAmplitudeIn gives C.IsGE a by testing the monoidal unit. Transfer it to P using the model isomorphism and isGE_Q_obj_iff. For each test module F, use QObjTensorSingleFunctorObjIso for this K-flat P and whiskerRightIso of its model isomorphism to transfer (hTor F).1 to (P tensor F).IsGE a. Thus P tensor F is exact at a-1. ObjectProperty.flat_opcycles_of_exactAt makes P.opcycles a flat. These are applications of proved upstream generic tools, with no new gap.

The cokernel map P.X a to P.opcycles a is surjective. Its kernel equals the range of the preceding differential by opcyclesIsCokernel and ShortComplex.moduleCat_exact_iff_range_eq_ker; this range is finitely generated since P.X (a-1) is finite (Submodule.fg_range). Module.finitePresentation_of_projective makes the finite-free source finitely presented, and Module.finitePresentation_of_surjective gives finite presentation of P.opcycles a. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-flat-module-projective] to this flat finitely presented bottom term.

Take the actual good truncation E = P.truncGE a. Below a its terms are zero; at a they are isomorphic to the bottom cokernel; above a they are isomorphic to the finite-free terms of P. Transfer Module.Finite and Module.Projective along these explicit linear equivalences. E is zero above c: at a use the epimorphism from the zero source P.X a if c<a, and above a use the original upper bound. The canonical map P.πTruncGE a is a quasi-isomorphism because P.IsGE a. Its Q-image is therefore an isomorphism; inverse it and compose with Q.obj P isomorphic to C. This gives exactly the unchanged existential conclusion, including the case c<a.

lean.statement: theorem isPerfect_of_pseudoCoherent_finiteTorAmplitude {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ModuleCat.{u} R)] (C : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} R)) (hPC : IsPseudoCoherent C) (hTor : ∃ a b : ℤ, a ≤ b ∧ torAmplitudeIn (ModuleCat.{u} R) a b C) : ∃ P : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ, (∃ a b : ℤ, ∀ n : ℤ, n < a ∨ b < n → IsZero (P.X n)) ∧ (∀ n : ℤ, Module.Finite R (P.X n)) ∧ (∀ n : ℤ, Module.Projective R (P.X n)) ∧ Nonempty (Q.obj P ≅ C)
